solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Secretive about explosive used to capture diamonds

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning

indicators.note: the explosive's letters are used to hold the gems, closing around them

parts.note: TNT is the common explosive trinitrotoluene
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone close-mouthed about the explosives deployed in a diamond heist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to capture' signals insertion: the gem slang goes inside the explosive, with 'about' placed first. Ice is underworld slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticent people keep their thoughts to themselves, which is being secretive or reserved.

clue.text: Republican given honour and ceremonial dress

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A Republican politician receives an honour and dresses up for the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is an honour awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A robe is a long formal garment worn on ceremonial occasions by judges, academics and peers.

clue.text: Mean to entertain cricket side in the near future?

indicators.note: the stingy word plays host to the cricket term, holding it inside

parts.note: a mean person is tight with money
the on side is one half of a cricket field, also called leg side

explanation.surface: A stingy person reluctantly hosts the cricket team sometime soon.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: This evening is a time very close at hand, hence the question mark for a loose fit.

clue.text: Peevish little person wrapping last of this embroidery

indicators.note: the two words together enclose the letter between them

parts.note: cross means irritable or peevish
titch is British slang for a small person

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word this is taken

explanation.surface: A grumpy small person wraps up the end of a needlework project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapping' signals that the two words together enclose the single letter, which sits at their join. Titch is British informal for a very small person.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-stitch is a style of needlework in which X-shaped stitches form a pattern.

clue.text: Unused vessel in Notts town

parts.note: something unused is new
Noah's ark was a vessel or ship

explanation.surface: A brand-new boat is moored in a Nottinghamshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts is short for Nottinghamshire, an English county; Newark-on-Trent is a market town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Newark is a market town on the River Trent in Nottinghamshire, England.

clue.text: Electronically summon boy attendant

definitions.meaning: to call someone by bleeper or ...
a young servant or attendant, as at a wedding or in a hotel

explanation.surface: Buzz the young lad who serves you.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to call via a pager device and a young male servant.

clue.text: Panic US city raised over weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second
in a down entry the city's letters are lifted, so read bottom to top

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: Fear spreads as an American city takes up arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is a sudden fear or anxiety, much like panic.

clue.text: Physical activity cut out without hesitation

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the cutting word goes around

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A workout dropped from the schedule without a moment's pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so it signals one piece enclosing the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise is bodily exertion done for health or fitness.

clue.text: Instrument little woman placed at end of bar

indicators.note: the girl's name goes after the word for bar

parts.note: to bar is to ban
Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A musician's wife sits at the far end of the pub counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little woman' points to Jo of Louisa May Alcott's Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: The banjo is a stringed musical instrument with a round drum-like body.

clue.text: A new ban upset one aspiring to greatness

indicators.note: the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A would-be celebrity is annoyed by a newly imposed ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A wannabe is someone who wants to be famous or successful, an aspirant.

clue.text: Casual attitude of church fellow in north once

indicators.note: the churchman sits inside the combined letters

parts.note: taken as written
Alan is a man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: A clergyman's laid-back manner up north in former times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals that the church abbreviation and the man's name together sit inside the north abbreviation plus 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonchalance is a calm, unconcerned air, a casual attitude.

clue.text: Like good eating? Fantastic roast coming!

indicators.note: the letters become fantastic, wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner enthuses that a wonderful roast dinner is on its way.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomic relates to gastronomy, the art of fine food and good eating.

clue.text: Devise method to make opening in deck

parts.note: to hatch a plan is to devise it
a way is a method

explanation.surface: A sailor works out how to cut a hole in a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchway is a trapdoor-like opening in a ship's deck leading below.

clue.text: Canny as boy king, Egyptian leader

parts.note: Tutankhamun, often Tut, was Egypt's boy king

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A young pharaoh was shrewd, as befits an Egyptian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute and canny both mean shrewd and quick to see an advantage.

clue.text: Section of oratorio or such? Could be

indicators.note: the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A musician wonders what part of a sacred work this might be.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio's sung parts include choral numbers sung by the whole choir.

clue.text: Old Asian port managed by stupid person?

parts.note: to have run something is to have managed it
a goon is a stupid person

explanation.surface: An ancient harbour was run by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangoon is the former name of Yangon, in Myanmar (Burma).
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon is the old name of Yangon, the chief seaport of Myanmar.

clue.text: Unproductive nobleman, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word for nobleman, said out loud, gives another word

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A lazy aristocrat, or so it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren land or effort yields nothing, so it is unproductive.

clue.text: Family emblem dropped to the ground? That makes us dejected

parts.note: a crest is a heraldic device of a family
something fallen has dropped to the floor

explanation.surface: The family coat of arms falls down, leaving everyone downcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Crestfallen describes someone sad and disappointed, deflated like a lowered crest.

clue.text: Woman abandoning husband in compound

indicators.note: the woman leaves her husband behind, so his letter is dropped

parts.note: Esther is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman walks out on her husband and moves into a walled compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a walled enclosure; it is a chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Esters are chemical compounds formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Governor entertains Queen in this place

indicators.note: the governor's letters play host to the queen's

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of a governor
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A colonial governor hosts the Queen at his residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Governors are addressed as His Excellency, HE; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a crossword staple for Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Here means at or in this location.

clue.text: Observer's friendly greeting to listener?

definitions.note: Observer's is read as Observer is, so the noun is the definition

indicators.note: the greeting heard by a listener sounds like a different word

parts.note: wotcher is a cockney greeting, from what cheer

explanation.surface: A newspaper's cheery hello to its readers and radio audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Wotcher is a London cockney greeting meaning hello.
explanation.definitionFit: A watcher is one who looks on, an observer.

clue.text: Police informer carrying old rope

indicators.note: the informer holds the abbreviation inside

parts.note: a nose is slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A police snitch carries an ancient rope around.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot.

clue.text: Quadrangle where low cart is reversing

indicators.note: the cart backs up, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a dray is a low flat cart for heavy loads

explanation.surface: A courtyard where a brewer's cart is backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: A dray is a low cart traditionally used by brewers.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is an enclosed open area, as a quadrangle is.

clue.text: Feelers put out by worker backing English girl

parts.note: the ant is the classic worker in crosswords

indicators.note: the letters are turned back to front

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An insect worker extends its feelers in support of an English girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Antennae are the sensory feelers on an insect's head.
